## Purpose and public entry points
Crawlee is a TypeScript/Node.js monorepo for reliable web scraping and browser automation. Consumers normally install the umbrella `crawlee` package, which re-exports crawler families and core APIs; packages can also be used independently. Main entry points: `packages/crawlee/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/index.ts`, and the project-bootstrap/run CLI at `packages/cli/src/index.ts`.

## Core crawl orchestration
`BasicCrawler` is the execution foundation: it consumes requests, invokes user handlers, applies retries/error handling, and coordinates crawl lifecycle. Shared request models, routing, events, logging, configuration, statistics, and crawler extensions live in core. Autoscaling dynamically adjusts work based on CPU, memory, and event-loop signals.
- `packages/basic-crawler/src/internals/basic-crawler.ts`
- `packages/core/src/request.ts`
- `packages/core/src/autoscaling/autoscaled_pool.ts`

## Request discovery and scheduling
A crawl starts with supplied URLs or request lists, then handlers can discover and enqueue links. Request queues/lists provide persistent scheduling, deduplication, and breadth/depth-oriented traversal; sitemap lists are another input source. This is the primary feedback loop: fetch/process → extract links → normalize/filter → enqueue → next request.
- `packages/core/src/enqueue_links/enqueue_links.ts`
- `packages/core/src/storages/request_queue.ts`
- `packages/core/src/storages/sitemap_request_list.ts`

## Crawler execution variants
Specialized packages implement a common crawler-facing model over distinct acquisition/rendering strategies: raw HTTP, Cheerio DOM parsing, JSDOM/LinkeDOM DOM emulation, and browser-driven Playwright/Puppeteer. The browser crawlers add page/context semantics and launchers; Playwright also has adaptive rendering selection. HTTP clients are abstracted so crawler implementations can use built-in or custom transport.
- `packages/http-crawler/src/internals/http-crawler.ts`
- `packages/cheerio-crawler/src/internals/cheerio-crawler.ts`
- `packages/playwright-crawler/src/internals/playwright-crawler.ts`

## Browser lifecycle, identity, and network boundary
Browser-based crawlers delegate browser creation and reuse to BrowserPool. Plugins/controllers isolate Playwright and Puppeteer integration; launch contexts, proxy servers, proxy anonymization, and fingerprinting hooks sit at the browser/network boundary. External browser runtimes are Playwright and Puppeteer, with support evidenced for Chromium and Firefox; Stagehand is an additional AI-oriented crawler integration.
- `packages/browser-pool/src/browser-pool.ts`
- `packages/browser-pool/src/abstract-classes/browser-plugin.ts`
- `packages/stagehand-crawler/src/internals/stagehand-crawler.ts`

## State, outputs, sessions, and proxies
Core storage abstractions expose datasets for records, key-value stores for files/state, and request sources. The default local implementation is `memory-storage`, which supports in-memory and filesystem-backed resource clients; an alternate storage client can represent cloud-backed services such as Apify platform storage. Sessions retain cookies/identity and combine with proxy configuration for rotation and block recovery.
- `packages/core/src/storages/storage_manager.ts`
- `packages/memory-storage/src/memory-storage.ts`
- `packages/core/src/session_pool/session_pool.ts`

## Delivery and operational surfaces
The repo ships npm packages, a CLI that creates/runs generated projects, templates with Dockerfiles, and a Docusaurus documentation website served through Nginx deployment automation. Runtime baseline is Node.js 16+. External operational targets include npm publishing, Apify platform deployment, Docker, AWS/GCP deployment guidance, and target websites/proxies.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/CreateProjectCommand.ts`
- `packages/templates/templates/playwright-ts/Dockerfile`
- `website/docusaurus.config.js`
